One side in this battle featured several units that had been in French service, such as the John Drummond-commanded Royal ?ossois, while the other had been augmented a few months before by a force of five thousand Hessians led by Prince Frederick. In this battle, the African Hunters attempted to scale a fort defending the namesake site. One side in this battle attacked at the Garita del Peaje. This man led the "Thundering Legion" against the Quadi. In the aftermath of this battle, the losing commander was sent to Prote and his wife was committed to a nunnery. Actions perpetrated by one side of this conflict prompted the formation of the Fawcett Comission.
